candidates.source_name: Ephrem the Syrian / Commentary on Deuteronomy
candidates.source_attribution: Ephrem the Syrian, Commentary on Deuteronomy, on 5:1-21. NPNF Series 2, vol. 13. PD.
candidates.draft_body:
Ephrem the Syrian Commentary on Deuteronomy (c. 365 AD)

On the prologue to the Decalogue's restatement — 'I am the Lord thy God, which brought thee out of the land of Egypt, from the house of bondage' (Deu 5:6) — Ephrem reads the placement of the redemption-formula BEFORE the commandments as the canonical anchor of the order-of-salvation: grace precedes obligation, the Exodus precedes Sinai. The Decalogue is given to a people already redeemed, not to a people earning redemption. Tewahedo catechetical theology cites Deu 5:6 as the canonical Old-Testament anchor for the order baptism-precedes-commandments: the catechumen is delivered from Egypt (baptism) BEFORE receiving the Tewahedo moral-life formation.
